title: Longest Common Subsequence
description: Given two strings, return the length of their longest common subsequence: the longest sequence of characters appearing in both in the same relative order, not necessarily contiguously.

reference.use_case: Finding the longest sequence of elements that appear in the same order in two versions of a file, to show what stayed the same and what changed.
system_examples: diff and Git — computing line-level differences between file versions (Myers' algorithm solves the closely related shortest-edit-script problem)
Bioinformatics — comparing DNA and protein sequences
reference.explanation: dp[i][j] = dp[i−1][j−1] + 1 when characters match, else max(dp[i−1][j], dp[i][j−1]), in O(m·n). LCS is the theoretical basis of diff: lines outside the LCS are exactly the insertions and deletions in a patch.
